name.zh-Hant: 加拿大洛磯山脈（露易絲湖）
name.zh-Hans: 加拿大落基山脉（露易丝湖）

airspace.zh: 加拿大國家公園管理局（Parks Canada）規定，所有國家公園都禁止休閒用途的無人機；未經許可在公園內操作無人機，最高可處25,000加元罰款。只有資源管理、公共安全、執法或公園管理等用途，才可能由園長核發許可。實際飛行前請先查詢加拿大運輸部與公園的規定。
airspace.en: Parks Canada prohibits recreational drone flying at all its places; operating a drone in a park without a permit can bring a fine of up to $25,000. The superintendent may permit drones only for resource management, public safety, law enforcement or park administration. Check Transport Canada and park rules before any real flight.

victoria.note: Glacier above the head of the lake; approximate

title.en: A Railway and a National Park

tagline.zh-Hant: 1882年的湖、1883年的溫泉、1885年加拿大第一座國家公園
tagline.en: A lake in 1882, hot springs in 1883, Canada's first national park in 1885

zh: 斯通尼族稱這座湖為「小魚之湖」。
早在歐洲人到來以前，原住民就熟悉這片山區。
en: The Stoney Nakoda call it Ho-run-num-nay, the Lake of the Little Fishes.
Indigenous peoples knew these mountains long before Europeans came.

zh: 1882年，斯通尼族嚮導艾德溫·杭特帶著湯姆·威爾遜來到湖邊。
威爾遜是第一位來到這裡的非原住民。
en: In 1882 the Stoney Nakoda guide Edwin Hunter led Tom Wilson to the shore.
Wilson was the first non-Indigenous visitor.

zh: 威爾遜起初把它叫作「翡翠湖」。
後來改以路易絲公主命名，她是維多利亞女王的女兒。
en: Wilson first called it Emerald Lake.
It was later named for Princess Louise, Queen Victoria's daughter.

zh: 當時，加拿大太平洋鐵路正要穿越洛磯山脈。
路線選在踢馬隘口翻越大陸分水嶺。
en: At the time, the Canadian Pacific Railway was pushing through the Rockies.
Its route crossed the Continental Divide at Kicking Horse Pass.

zh: 1858年，探險家詹姆斯·赫克特在這裡被馬踢傷。
隘口因此得名「踢馬」。
en: In 1858 the explorer James Hector was kicked by his horse here,
and the pass took its name from that.

zh: 隘口西側的「大坡」，是北美最陡的幹線鐵路之一。
1909年，鐵路在山裡挖出兩座螺旋隧道，降低坡度。
en: West of the pass, the Big Hill was among the steepest main-line grades in North America.
In 1909 two spiral tunnels were cut into the mountains to ease it.

zh: 火車在山體裡繞一圈，從自己的上方或下方再出來。
長列車有時能同時看到頭尾從兩個洞口出現。
en: Trains loop inside the mountain and emerge above or below themselves.
A long train can be seen leaving one portal while still entering another.

zh: 1883年，三名鐵路工人在東邊的硫磺山發現溫泉。
這件事，促成了加拿大第一座國家公園。
en: In 1883 three railway workers claimed hot springs on Sulphur Mountain to the east.
That claim led to Canada's first national park.

zh: 1885年，政府劃出26平方公里的溫泉保留區。
1887年擴大為665平方公里的洛磯山公園，即今天的班夫。
en: In 1885 the government set aside a 26 square kilometre hot springs reserve.
In 1887 it grew to 665 km² as Rocky Mountains Park, today Banff National Park.

zh: 鐵路公司在湖的東岸蓋起旅館。
二十世紀初改建成今天的露易絲湖城堡飯店。
en: The railway company built a hotel on the eastern shore,
rebuilt in the early 20th century as the Chateau Lake Louise.

zh: 1899年，湯姆·威爾遜開出通往夢蓮湖的第一條步道。
1924年，車輛終於可以開上一條簡陋的道路。
en: In 1899 Tom Wilson cut the first trail to Moraine Lake.
By 1924 a rough road let vehicles in.

zh: 1969年，夢蓮湖的景色印上加拿大二十元紙鈔。
這片山谷，成了全國熟悉的風景。
en: In 1969 Moraine Lake appeared on Canada's twenty-dollar note.
The valley became a view the whole country knew.

zh: 1909年，古生物學家查爾斯·沃爾科特在幽鶴發現伯吉斯頁岩。
它後來成為世界聞名的化石產地。
en: In 1909 the palaeontologist Charles Walcott found the Burgess Shale in Yoho.
It became one of the most famous fossil sites in the world.

zh: 1984年，加拿大洛磯山脈的國家公園群列入世界遺產。
班夫、幽鶴、賈斯珀和庫特尼國家公園都在其中。
en: In 1984 the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks joined the World Heritage List,
among them Banff, Yoho, Jasper and Kootenay national parks.

zh: 一條鐵路帶來了旅館、遊客和國家公園。
加拿大的國家公園體系，就從這片山區開始。
en: A railway brought hotels, visitors and a national park.
Canada's national park system began in these mountains.

tagline.zh-Hant: 原住民的山、鐵路旅館、山中茶屋與紙鈔上的湖
tagline.en: Indigenous mountains, railway hotels, a tea house and a lake on a banknote

zh: 班夫國家公園位在多個原住民族的傳統領域裡。
包括庫特尼、斯通尼、布拉德、皮根、錫克西卡和楚提納族。
en: Banff National Park lies in the traditional territory of several First Nations:
the Kootenay, Stoney, Blood, Peigan, Siksika and Tsuut'ina.

zh: 露易絲湖的斯通尼名字，是「小魚之湖」。
1882年，正是斯通尼嚮導帶外人來到這裡。
en: The Stoney name for Lake Louise means Lake of the Little Fishes.
In 1882 it was a Stoney guide who led an outsider here.

zh: 湖東岸的城堡飯店，由加拿大太平洋鐵路公司興建。
鐵路旅館，把歐洲式的山居度假帶進洛磯山。
en: The Chateau on the eastern shore was built by the Canadian Pacific Railway.
Railway hotels brought European-style mountain holidays to the Rockies.

zh: 許多遊客清晨來到湖邊，等待湖面最平靜的時刻。
山影倒映在湖上，是露易絲湖最常見的明信片。
en: Many visitors come at dawn for the stillest water,
when the mountains mirrored in the lake make the classic postcard.

zh: 沿著步道往上爬，可以到達艾格尼絲湖。
湖邊有一座山中茶屋，登山客在這裡歇腳。
en: A trail climbs from the shore to Lake Agnes,
where a mountain tea house gives walkers a rest.

zh: 茶屋只能靠步行抵達。
補給有時要靠直升機送上山。
en: The tea house can be reached only on foot.
Supplies sometimes come up by helicopter.

zh: 夢蓮湖曾印在1969年的加拿大二十元紙鈔上。
「十峰山谷」，因此成為全國熟悉的風景。
en: Moraine Lake was pictured on Canada's twenty-dollar note of 1969.
The Valley of the Ten Peaks became a view the whole nation knew.

zh: 1899年，威爾考克斯形容第一眼看到它的時刻，
是他一生中「最快樂的半小時」。
en: In 1899 Wilcox called his first sight of it
the happiest half-hour of his life.

zh: 湖邊的山莊由建築師亞瑟·埃里克森設計。
它被要求與自然融為一體，每天接待約四千名遊客。
en: Its lodge was designed by the architect Arthur Erickson
to blend with nature, while serving about 4,000 visitors a day.

zh: 九月下旬，落葉松谷的高山落葉松轉成金黃色。
這是一年中最多人上山的時節之一。
en: In late September the alpine larches of Larch Valley turn gold,
one of the busiest times on the trail.

zh: 冬天，露易絲湖結冰。
湖面成為溜冰場，四周還有冰攀、雪鞋與狗拉雪橇。
en: In winter Lake Louise freezes.
It becomes a skating rink, with ice climbing, snowshoeing and dog sledding around it.

zh: 觀景台上，遊客等著看火車穿過螺旋隧道。
鐵路本身，也成了一種觀光。
en: At the viewpoint, people wait to watch trains wind through the Spiral Tunnels.
The railway itself became an attraction.

zh: 塔卡考的名字，來自克里語，意思是「真壯觀」。
一個詞，就說盡了眼前的瀑布。
en: Takakkaw comes from a Cree word meaning "it is magnificent".
One word says all there is to say about the falls.

zh: 從原住民的山、鐵路帶來的旅人，
到今天每年湧入的遊客，這些湖一直被人們珍惜。
en: From Indigenous mountains to railway travellers
to the crowds of today, these lakes have always been treasured.

title.zh-Hant: 灰熊、落葉松與野生動物天橋

tagline.zh-Hant: 53種哺乳動物，與世界知名的公路生態廊道
tagline.en: 53 mammal species, and a famous system of highway wildlife crossings

zh: 班夫國家公園面積6,641平方公里。
園內記錄了53種哺乳動物和至少280種鳥類。
en: Banff National Park covers 6,641 square kilometres.
It records 53 species of mammals and at least 280 of birds.

zh: 灰熊、黑熊、美洲獅、麋鹿、駝鹿和大角羊都住在這裡。
這是北美最完整的山地生態系之一。
en: Grizzly and black bears, cougars, elk, moose and bighorn sheep live here.
It is one of the most complete mountain ecosystems in North America.

zh: 橫貫加拿大公路穿過公園。
1981年起，公路從兩線道拓寬成四線道。
en: The Trans-Canada Highway runs through the park.
From 1981 it was widened from two lanes to four.

zh: 為了讓動物安全通過，公路沿線蓋了44座動物通道。
其中38座是地下涵洞，6座是天橋。
en: To let animals cross safely, 44 wildlife crossings were built along it:
38 underpasses and six overpasses.

zh: 1996年到2012年，十一種大型哺乳動物使用通道超過十五萬次。
圍欄加上通道，讓動物與車輛的碰撞減少八成以上。
en: From 1996 to 2012, eleven large mammal species used them more than 150,000 times.
Fences and crossings cut wildlife–vehicle collisions by over 80 per cent.

zh: 麋鹿和鹿的車禍，更減少了96%以上。
這套設計，後來成為世界各地參考的案例。
en: For elk and deer, collisions fell by more than 96 per cent.
The design has since been studied around the world.

zh: 落葉松谷長著高山落葉松。
它是少數會在秋天落葉的針葉樹。
en: Larch Valley is named for its alpine larches,
one of the few conifers that drop their needles in autumn.

zh: 九月下旬，整片山谷轉成金黃。
接著葉子落盡，迎接冬天。
en: In late September the whole valley turns gold,
then the needles fall before winter.

zh: 湖邊的森林，以雲杉和冷杉為主。
再往上，樹木逐漸稀少，換成高山草甸與岩石。
en: The lakeshore forest is mostly spruce and fir.
Higher up, trees thin out into alpine meadow and rock.

zh: 山谷裡的冰河，正在逐漸後退。
融水的多寡，決定了下游湖泊的顏色與水量。
en: The glaciers in the valley are slowly retreating.
How much they melt sets the colour and level of the lakes below.

zh: 冰河是這些湖泊的源頭。
冰河變小，湖的未來也會跟著改變。
en: The glaciers are where these lakes begin.
As the ice shrinks, the lakes will change with it.

zh: 幽鶴的翡翠湖，周圍是茂密的森林。
這裡也是駝鹿和熊出沒的地方。
en: Yoho's Emerald Lake is ringed by dense forest,
country where moose and bears roam.

zh: 塔卡考瀑布的水，來自上方冰原的融水。
夏天融冰最多時，水量最大。
en: Takakkaw Falls is fed by meltwater from the icefield above.
It runs fullest in summer, when the most ice melts.

zh: 從灰熊、麋鹿到金黃的落葉松，
班夫證明了人和野生動物，可以共用同一片山谷。
en: From grizzlies and elk to golden larches,
Banff shows that people and wildlife can share one valley.

tagline.zh-Hant: 岩粉染出的湖色、堰塞的湖，與分隔兩洋的隘口
tagline.en: Rock flour colours, a rockslide-dammed lake and a pass between two oceans

zh: 加拿大洛磯山脈裡的露易絲湖，湖面海拔1,750公尺。
湖長約兩公里，寬約五百公尺，最深七十公尺。
en: Lake Louise, in the Canadian Rockies, lies 1,750 metres above sea level.
It is about 2 km long, 500 m wide and up to 70 m deep.

zh: 湖水的青綠色，來自冰河融水帶來的岩粉。
極細的岩石粉末懸浮在水中，散射出這種顏色。
en: Its turquoise comes from rock flour carried in by glacial meltwater.
Fine particles of ground rock hang in the water and scatter this colour.

zh: 湖的盡頭，是維多利亞山與它的冰河。
冰河磨碎岩石，才有了岩粉。
en: At the head of the lake rise Mount Victoria and its glacier.
Grinding the rock, the ice makes the flour.

zh: 湖的主要水源，是上游的勒弗羅伊冰河。
冰河後退，留下了一路下降的山谷。
en: The lake is fed mainly by the Lefroy Glacier upstream.
As the ice retreated it left this stepped valley.

zh: 山坡上方的艾格尼絲湖，是一座冰斗湖。
冰河在山壁上挖出的凹地，積水成湖。
en: Lake Agnes, higher on the slope, is a cirque lake.
Water filled a hollow the ice scooped from the mountainside.

zh: 南邊的夢蓮湖，位在十峰山谷。
1899年，探險家華特·威爾考克斯為它命名。
en: To the south, Moraine Lake lies in the Valley of the Ten Peaks.
The explorer Walter Wilcox named it in 1899.

zh: 他以為湖是被冰磧堵住的，所以叫它「冰磧湖」。
後來發現，堵住湖口的其實是山崩落下的岩堆。
en: He thought a glacial moraine dammed it, hence the name.
In fact the dam is a pile of rock from a landslide.

zh: 湖後並排著十座山峰。
它們屬於分隔亞伯達與卑詩兩省的山脈。
en: Ten peaks stand in a row behind the lake.
They belong to the range that divides Alberta from British Columbia.

zh: 坦普爾山海拔3,544公尺，是這一帶最高的山。
山上的岩層，是古老的海底沉積。
en: Mount Temple, at 3,544 metres, is the highest peak around Lake Louise.
Its layers were laid down on ancient sea floors.

zh: 踢馬隘口位在北美大陸分水嶺上。
東側的水流向哈德遜灣，西側的水流向太平洋。
en: Kicking Horse Pass lies on the Continental Divide.
Water on the east drains to Hudson Bay; on the west, to the Pacific.

zh: 越過隘口，就從亞伯達省進入卑詩省。
西側是幽鶴國家公園。
en: Cross the pass and Alberta becomes British Columbia.
On the west side lies Yoho National Park.

zh: 幽鶴的塔卡考瀑布，從冰原融水直落山谷。
它是加拿大最高的瀑布之一。
en: Yoho's Takakkaw Falls drops meltwater from an icefield into the valley.
It is one of Canada's highest waterfalls.

zh: 山脊上的伯吉斯頁岩，保存了約五億年前的海洋生物。
連柔軟的身體構造，都留在岩石裡。
en: On the ridge, the Burgess Shale preserves sea life from about half a billion years ago,
down to the soft parts of their bodies.

zh: 翡翠湖同樣由冰河融水供給。
湖岸的森林，倒映在綠色的湖面上。
en: Emerald Lake is also fed by glacial meltwater.
Its forested shores reflect in the green water.

zh: 從正上方看，冰河、河流和湖泊連成一串。
水從冰河出發，一路流進湖裡。
en: From straight above, glacier, stream and lake form one chain.
Water sets out from the ice and runs into the lake.

zh: 冰河磨出的岩粉、山崩堵出的湖、分隔兩洋的隘口，
洛磯山脈的地景，是冰與岩石共同寫成的。
en: Rock flour ground by ice, a lake dammed by a landslide, a pass between two oceans:
the Rockies are written by ice and stone together.
